results.question: How should I take NOTCAM dark frames for my observations?
results.answer:
### Darks

The NOTCam darks are poorly understood, see the  [NOTCam User's Guide](http://www.not.iac.es/instruments/notcam/guide/observe.html#darks)
for a comment. By using differential flats and sky-subtraction, the dark is
automatically subtracted out, and you should not need to take darks for
broad-band imaging. Darks are useful to estimate hot pixels, however, which
vary with exposure time. Take darks with the same exposure time and readout
mode as your observations.

[obs@selena][NOTCAM]$ notcam.dark *t*

[obs@selena][NOTCAM]$ notcam.mdark *t N*

[obs@selena][NOTCAM]$ notcam.dframe *t N*

NB! Since the array needs time to stabilize on the low count levels, it is
recommended to take N > 3 subsequent darks of the same integration
time, and preferrably disregard the first one(s).

[D-9e122ed87d2b89a6-C35]

results.question: How do I align two objects on an ALFOSC slit using slitrot?
results.answer:
1. Take a short exposure of the field without slit/grism,
2. Give the command
        **slitrot**
   in the sequencer terminal.
3. In the DS9 image display point at the 2 objects following the
   instruction given by the
   **slitrot** program.
4. The **slitrot** program will then print the offset to the
   current field angle on the display, both for vertical and for
   horizontal slits.
5. Set the appropriate rotator angle with the TCS command:

**field-rotation**
    where
   new\_field is the recommended rotator angle for the slit
   orientation used.

6. Then put one of the objects, and consequently also the other, on
   the slit (see  ["Positioning a star on the
   slit"](slitpos.html)).
7. In case you want to put the two objects centered on
   the CCD, proceed with a  **teloffset** along the slit.

[D-df839f142ee21e5a-C0] [D-df839f142ee21e5a-C1]

results.question: How can I download my observing data from the NOT data server?
results.answer:
## NOT data server

Only principal investigators (PIs) have direct access to their data on the data server. The principal investigators can grant access to their data by generating and distributing a shared link. Details on how to do so can be found in the following instructions.

First of all, you need a user account to access your data. If you already have an account on our OB generator, you do not need to register a new one, your username and password are valid on both the OB Generator and the data server. Otherwise, please create an account [here](http://www.not.iac.es/observing/forms/ob/user_add.php) and note that it is **essential** to provide the same email address as indicated in the proposal submission in order to link your account to your data.

[How to get my data?](#get_data)

[How to share the data with my team?](#share_data)

---

## How to get my data?

2. Access to the **NOT data server** ([https://data.not.iac.es/](https://data.not.iac.es)) and log in. In case you do not remember your username and/or password, contact with us at **obsupport [at] not.iac.es**
3. Images on data server are sorted by period, proposal number, night and instrument. Those directories are under an unique shared folder named proposal that is indeed the home directory for all users, so after clicking on **"File Station"** icon a window will be opened from which you can navigate through the directory structure. Of course, you are only allowed to access the directories containing data related with your proposals (other proposal directories are not even shown).

4. Once the instrument directory root for a given night have been reached, you will find all raw files taken that night with said instrument and some of the following folders (if applicable):
   > **calib** - *daily instrument calibration frames*
   >
   > **quicklook** - *ALFOSC and NOTCam quicklook spectra*
   >
   > **reduced** - *FIES spectra reduction files (Thorium-Argon, blaze correction, wavelenght and merge)*
5. You can download a single file by just double clicking on it or by choosing "Download" on the context menu (right clicking). This second way also leave you to select several files (by holding down the Shift key) or even entire folders, which are compressed before downloading. In fact, the most common use case is to download a ZIP file with all images taken in a night.

[D-599ab3becaa3ed21-C1] [D-599ab3becaa3ed21-C2] [D-599ab3becaa3ed21-C3]

results.question: Describe the process an observer must follow to interactively identify a target for spectroscopy during an Observing Block (OB) execution.
results.answer:
ALFOSC operator-guide instructions:

The first interaction needed is to confirm the guiding. For Alfosc imaging OB's no other interaction is needed. For Alfosc spectroscopy OBs, the script will then start by taking an acquisition image, and you will have to identify the desired target in the field, by placing the mouse on the target and pressing a+q for point sources or x+q for extended sources. Once identified, the script will take another acquisition image and ask to identify the target again in the same way. Finally, the OB will take an image of the slit. If the star is there and the acquisition is done correctly, the OB will ask you to press enter TWICE. Otherwise, you can repeat the acquisition. Once these interactions have finished, the observations of the spectra will start here. For other instrument interactions (after confirming guiding) may differ, but there will be always explanation in sequencer. [D-c4a919f6f9136951-C88]

results.question: Describe the process an observer must follow to interactively identify a target for spectroscopy during an Observing Block (OB) execution.
results.answer:
ALFOSC operator-guide instructions:

The first interaction needed is to confirm the guiding. For Alfosc imaging OB's no other interaction is needed. For Alfosc spectroscopy OBs, the script will then start by taking an acquisition image, and you will have to identify the desired target in the field, by placing the mouse on the target and pressing a+q for point sources or x+q for extended sources. Once identified, the script will take another acquisition image and ask to identify the target again in the same way. Finally, the OB will take an image of the slit. If the star is there and the acquisition is done correctly, the OB will ask you to press enter TWICE. Otherwise, you can repeat the acquisition. Once these interactions have finished, the observations of the spectra will start here. For other instrument interactions (after confirming guiding) may differ, but there will be always explanation in sequencer. [D-c4a919f6f9136951-C88]
results.reference: The observer identifies the target on the acquisition image by placing the mouse cursor over it and pressing a+q for point sources or x+q for extended sources.

results.question: Under what specific weather conditions (wind speed and humidity) must the telescope be closed immediately?
results.answer:
Humidity : > 90% - Close telescope; After 20min < 90% the telescope can be reopened. [D-3984d286e5e844ca-C27]

Wind : 12 m/s - Close sideports and lower hatch [D-3984d286e5e844ca-C27]

Wind : 20 m/s - Close telescope [D-3984d286e5e844ca-C27]
results.reference: The telescope must be closed if the humidity reaches 90% or the wind speed reaches 20 m/s.

results.question: What should an observer do if the ALFOSC UIF fails to start with an error message?
results.answer: Please provide the exact error message. The cited guide gives a conditional remedy for "The ALFOSC UIF did not start. Restart the observing system."; an unspecified startup error does not establish that this remedy applies. [D-c4a919f6f9136951-C125]
